# P1 roster — derived from the K x86-64 semantics

Plan v1 §2 names the K semantics (NCSA, © 2019 UIUC) as the COVERAGE TARGET
LIST; §5 prices P1 as an executor wave over that list "machine-partitioned
into batches of like forms". This table is that partition. It is generated by
`scripts/k_roster.py` and regenerated in CI, so it cannot drift from K's tree
or from an editor's memory of it.

## What the numbers are

| | |
|---|---|
| K commit the roster is derived from | `592380aea048` |
| K variants in the four user-level directories | 3063 |
| files filed in two of them, counted once | 0 |
| dropped as SIMD/FP (P2, not P1) | 1665 |
| scalar-integer variants kept | 1398 |
| **FORMS** (base mnemonic × operand shape, widths folded) | **525** |
| base mnemonics | 184 |
| of those, not already in the P0 roster | 135 |
| families (= batches) | 61 |

Operand shapes are written **destination first**, which is the order K's
filenames use (`addq_m64_r64` is the rule `addq %r64, (mem)`), so `m,r`
means a register source stored to a memory destination.

A FORM is one base mnemonic at one operand shape, with the widths folded
together — the same granularity the P0 coverage table counts in, where 20
mnemonics made 43 forms. The width is a datum on the instruction
(docs/DECISIONS.md D4), so `addb`/`addw`/`addl`/`addq` at `r,r` is ONE form
and four K variants. `width_conflict=1` marks a form whose widths dispose of
their flags differently in K — a finding, and there are 4 of them.

## The family key, and why it is computed

`flags|reads|dest`, where `flags` is one character per flag in the order
CF PF AF ZF SF OF DF:

| char | meaning |
|---|---|
| `-` | K does not write the flag |
| `x` | K writes a computed value |
| `0` / `1` | K writes the constant 0 / 1 |
| `u` | **K writes `undefMInt`** — K's own reading of an Intel-undefined flag |

⛔ **WHAT THE `u` COLUMN DOES NOT SAY, measured rather than assumed.** K
marks a flag `undefMInt` only when it is undefined UNCONDITIONALLY. A flag
the SDM leaves undefined only for SOME operand values is a computed
expression in K like any other: `shlq $imm8, %r64` contains no `undefMInt`
at all, though the SDM leaves its CF undefined when the masked count
reaches the operand width, its OF undefined when the count is not 1, and
its AF undefined whenever the count is non-zero. So `k_undef` is a LOWER
BOUND on the undefined set, and for the shift group it is the empty set
while this model's is three state-dependent regions. A roster column that
looked authoritative here would have quietly argued for deleting P0's
shift oracle draws — which the P0 differential run measured as 694 real
declines-to-commit.

⭐ The `u` column is a THIRD INDEPENDENT READING of the undefined set. P0
derived its undefined regions from this model's two-oracle differential
(docs/DECISIONS.md D6) and cross-read them against the SDM and ACL2 x86isa.
K is a fourth party reading the same manual. Where `k_undef` and this
model's `undefinedFlags` disagree on a form, plan v1 §4.2 says that is a
FINDING — and having it in the roster puts the finding BEFORE the
implementation instead of after the differential run.

## Batch order

Families that WRITE FLAGS come first, then the largest first. Batch 1 is
therefore a flag-heavy batch and not the cheapest one available: a wave
priced on its easiest batch is priced wrong, and the price is the whole
reason the first batch is being run.

## Exclusions — the only hand judgements here

| what | why |
|---|---|
| `vzeroall` | AVX state instruction; no integer operand to filter on. P2. |
| `vzeroupper` | AVX state instruction; no integer operand to filter on. P2. |
| `cvt*` | SSE/AVX float<->integer conversion: reads or writes an XMM register. P2. |
| `vcvt*` | AVX float<->integer conversion: reads or writes an XMM register. P2. |
| any operand `xmm`/`ymm`/`zmm`/`mm`/`m128`/`m256`/`m512` | SIMD: plan v1 §5 P2. |

Dropped, by reason: SIMD operand (P2) 1549, float/vector conversion 114, named exclusion 2.
